reviewer_note: Independent review performed in a fresh session. This directory already contained a prior lane_l_review.json and lane_r_review.json (both verdict ACCEPT) -- those are treated as the composer's own untrusted claims, not as authority, per this task's mandate to independently re-derive the verdict rather than defer to them. This review found a structural defect in the Lane L artifact itself that both prior review files missed.

checks.detail: lane_l_candidate.md (434 bytes) does NOT contain README content. Its full contents are: 'Empty-patch ACCEPT. All 12 checked facts in facts.json are SUPPORTED (0 CONTRADICTED); the single UNVERIFIED fact (F-XLS-ODS-XLSB-UNSUPPORTED) is a negative/scope claim left untouched per the playbook... Per the playbook's fast path, the Lane L candidate is the live README unchanged... No lane_l_candidate.diff is produced for this reason.' This is a rationale/seal, not the README it claims to be. live_readme.md is 5432 bytes / 184 lines of actual README content. Compare the two other empty-patch-ACCEPT siblings reviewed in this same batch (aspose-3d-foss/Aspose.3D-FOSS-for-TypeScript, aspose-barcode-foss/Aspose.BarCode-FOSS-for-Python): in both of those, lane_l_candidate.md is a byte-identical COPY of live_readme.md's actual content, verified with `cmp`. Here it is not -- `cmp live_readme.md lane_l_candidate.md` differs completely; the file never received the README text it was supposed to carry.

The pre-existing lane_l_review.json in this directory (verdict ACCEPT) checked only facts.json's claim dispositions (C1-C4) and never opened or inspected the actual bytes of lane_l_candidate.md -- it describes the candidate only through the facts.json narration ('empty-patch is the correct Lane L output'), not through direct inspection of what the file contains. This is exactly the blind spot docs/MISSION_AUTHORITY.md's 'critical fact' section warns about: a reviewer that shares the producer's own untested assumption is not independent. This review opened the file directly and found the mismatch.

Independently spot-checked F-PDF-REQUIRES-SKIA (the most consequential SUPPORTED fact, a guarded-failure claim): re-fetched the behavior is consistent with the README's own PDF-support subsection text (skia-python required, pip install instructions given) -- the underlying facts.json content itself is not in question here; only the Lane L candidate artifact's construction is defective. All 12 facts are correctly dispositioned (11 SUPPORTED, 1 UNVERIFIED and correctly left uncorrected); 0 CONTRADICTED content facts, so an empty-patch Lane L (i.e. the live README unchanged) would have been the CORRECT target output -- it just was never actually produced in the file.

lane_r_candidate.md (235 lines) is a complete, standalone document, not a seal. Verified section-by-section against lane_r_plan.md's claims: Navigation and At a Glance are genuinely new (ADD, matching content_units.json), Features->Key Capabilities / Scope->Scope and Limitations / Examples and API->Documentation & Resources / Development->Development and Testing are renamed with bullet text retained verbatim (spot-checked: the 10 Key Capabilities bullets and 4 Scope bullets are character-identical to live_readme.md's Features and Scope bullets), and the Enterprise Edition cross-link paragraph is genuinely new (ADD). No bullet was dropped, reworded, or fact-wise altered.

F-STRUCTURAL-SKELETON-DIVERGES-FROM-FAMILY (CONTRADICTED, structural not factual) claims this is the only one of 7 Cells-family READMEs lacking Navigation/At-a-Glance/Enterprise-link. This is a comparative claim across repositories this review did not re-verify against all 6 siblings directly (out of scope for a single-repo review), but it is internally consistent: live_readme.md (read in full) genuinely has no Navigation section, no mermaid diagram, and no Enterprise Edition mention anywhere -- confirmed directly.

F-XLS-ODS-XLSB-UNSUPPORTED is UNVERIFIED; both lane_r_candidate.md's Scope bullet and the live README's Scope bullet state the same unverified negative claim unchanged -- not silently asserted as confirmed true or corrected as false.

findings.finding: lane_l_candidate.md is not a README. The file's entire content is a 5-line rationale paragraph explaining why an empty-patch outcome was chosen; it does not contain any of the actual live README's 184 lines / 5432 bytes of product documentation. This means the Lane L deliverable for this repository does not exist in usable form -- anyone opening lane_l_candidate.md expecting the Lane L candidate README would see only a meta-commentary note, not a document. This is a deterministic, reproducible defect (verified by direct file read and by `cmp` against live_readme.md, which shows no resemblance). The correct fix is mechanical: lane_l_candidate.md should be replaced with a verbatim copy of live_readme.md (as was correctly done for the sibling empty-patch cases aspose-3d-foss/Aspose.3D-FOSS-for-TypeScript and aspose-barcode-foss/Aspose.BarCode-FOSS-for-Python in this same batch) -- the rationale text belongs in review.json's verdict_rationale or a dedicated notes field, not in the candidate file itself. The pre-existing lane_l_review.json in this directory incorrectly verdicts this ACCEPT without ever inspecting the candidate file's actual bytes; that verdict should not be relied upon.

verdict_rationale: Lane R's candidate is sound: a real, complete, properly-sourced document whose structural divergence from the live README is evidence-backed and whose retained content is verbatim. Lane L's candidate was found defective (see findings) by the supervisor session 2026-10-21: lane_l_candidate.md replaced with a verbatim copy of live_readme.md (byte-identical, confirmed via `diff`), matching the two sibling empty-patch cases in this batch. Verdict updated from REJECT to ACCEPT after the fix; this is not a retroactive downgrade of the finding -- the finding stands as correctly identified and is marked 'fixed', not erased, per this project's AGENTS.md re-reporting discipline.
